bib.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Figs 1-9 are images (captions only).

question: How can an LLM planner be made reliable for long-horizon, state-dependent multi-task planning in open-world environments such as Minecraft?
hypothesis: Feeding execution descriptions back, having the LLM explain its own plan failures, and ranking parallel goals by predicted completion horizon will beat one-shot or feedback-only LLM planners.
contributions: DEPS: interactive Describe, Explain, Plan, Select planning with LLMs
Horizon-predictive goal selector that ranks parallel sub-goals by estimated steps to completion
Zero-shot multi-task agent for 70+ Minecraft tasks, nearly doubling overall success
Generalisation tests on ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation; first planning-based agent to reach ObtainDiamond

method.summary: A planner LLM (Codex) writes a Python-like plan with preconditions; a descriptor turns the Minecraft inventory/biome info into text on failure; the LLM explains the failure from few-shot demos and re-plans; a learned horizon-predictive selector orders parallel candidate goals; a behavior-cloned goal-conditioned controller executes goals.
method.task: LLM-based task planning for embodied agents (Minecraft, ALFWorld, tabletop)

datasets.name: Minecraft Task101 (71 hardest tasks from MCU SkillForgeChain, subset of MineDojo programmatic tasks)
datasets.size: 71 tasks in 8 meta groups (counts per group in Table 1: 14,12,7,6,9,7,13,1)
datasets.split: all evaluated; each run 30 times (at least 30 across world seeds)
datasets.preprocessing: Only the 'given nothing' condition kept; empty inventory, survival mode, axe given; random biome and spawn each run

datasets.name: Offline Minecraft trajectories for horizon selector and BC controller
datasets.source: not stated in this paper (controller from Cai et al. 2023, arXiv 2301.10034)
datasets.preprocessing: 42 discretised actions from MineDojo action space

models.name: code-davinci-02 (Codex)
models.architecture: OpenAI completion LLM, planner in Minecraft

other.note: max re-planning rounds about 7-8 due to token limit

models.name: text-davinci-03
models.architecture: OpenAI LLM; explainer in Minecraft, planner in ALFWorld, baselines GPT/CoT/IM

models.name: LLaMA2-13B finetuned on internet Minecraft text
Horizon-predictive selector (goal-sensitive Impala CNN)
models.architecture: Impala CNN backbone, may share backbone with controller

models.name: Goal-conditioned BC controller (Cai et al. 2023)
models.architecture: modified goal-sensitive Impala CNN; 262 goals; skill success 0.00-1.00 in Table 18

models.name: Sentence-BERT (goal parser fallback)

training.objective: Selector: negative log-likelihood -log mu(h_t(g)|s_t,g) of ground-truth horizon on offline trajectories; controller: imitation learning (behavior cloning)

other.note: LLM planner is not trained (no gradient updates); only selector, controller and the LLaMA2-13B finetune train, none with hyperparameters given

inference.max_tokens: limited by model context; Codex ~7-8 re-planning rounds
inference.prompting: Chat-style dialogue; 2 DEP demonstrations with Descriptor/Explainer/RePlanner turns; Python-like plan with step comments; explainer few-shot (3 examples)

other.hyperparameters: All LLM hyper-parameters (temperature, best_of) kept as default

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of episodes in which the task item is obtained within max steps

eval.protocol: Same demos, OpenAI LLM and controller for all baselines (baselines re-implemented for Minecraft); mean +- std across tasks in meta group; no significance tests

prompts.text: User: You are a helper agent in Minecraft. You need to generate the sequences of goals for a certain task in Minecraft. ... Descriptor: I succeed on step 1, 2, 3, but I fail on step 4 ... Explainer: Because mining cobblestone needs to use the tool wooden_pickaxe. User: Please fix the above errors and replan the task "obtain 1 stone_sword".
Here are some actions that the agent fails to perform in Minecraft. Please give the explanation of action execution failure according to the current inventory information of the agent.
Extract the action name, action type, goal object, tool and action rank from the input text.

limits: Relies on privately-held LLMs (GPT-3, Codex, ChatGPT); open LLaMA2 tested only on 4 simple tasks (Table 20)
Explicit step-by-step planning is a bottleneck for scaling; authors suggest amortising into an end-to-end policy
Fundamental planning challenges such as dead ends may not occur in the chosen environments
Controller is the main bottleneck: 0.59% ObtainDiamond with BC controller vs 60% with oracle
No selector training details (data size, optimizer, steps); no significance tests; Table 4/19 use unbounded rounds limited by tokens
Baselines re-implemented by the authors for Minecraft with prompt/feedback template choices; ALFWorld uses 10 tasks x 5 runs and tabletop 5 tasks (coarse percentages)
Codex (code-davinci-02) and text-davinci-03 are deprecated models

code.snippet: Description: dt = fDESC(st−1), Explanation: et = fEX(dt), Prompt: pt = CONCAT(pt−1, dt, et), Plan: Pt = fLM(pt), Goal: gt ∼ fS(Pt, st−1), Action: at ∼ π(at | st−1, gt)
